evidence.note: CLAIM: recorded ci gates can predict a selected run's wall time well enough to decide the suite slot; no per-test durations are stored (git grep: only pytest --durations as an ignored flag), but each ci gate records elapsed_s, waited_s, ci_scope.selected/always_s/ran/workers. MECHANISM: rate = (elapsed - waited - always_s) * workers / selected files; predicted = median(rate) * files / WK.compute(cfg, files).n, so load enters through the one governor. FALSIFIER: a per-run rate predicts no better than a constant, or a small unloaded run still predicts heavy. PROBE 1 (backtest of 200 recorded selected runs with a worker count, each predicted from up to 200 earlier ones, median/p90 relative error): constant 0.35/2.18, global rate 0.29/1.19, per-file attribution 0.28/1.11. Per-file is no better, so the global rate is used. PROBE 2 (real code on the real log: 6059 ci events, 200 measured, newest 50 median 184.2 worker-s/file, scan 0.6 ms; 192 cores): load/core 0.05: 3f 184s, 55f 211s, 100f 384s stay off the slot, 178f 683s takes it; 0.6: 55f 362s, 78f 513s stay, 100f 658s takes it; 0.75 and over: n=1, 3f 552s stays, 24f+ takes it. Falsifier not met. Default 600 s: selected wall p90 531 s, recorded full suite about 2000 s.

chunk_findings.detail: The guard `or not isinstance((scope.get("ran") or {}).get("selected"), bool)` only checks that `ci_scope.ran.selected` is a bool, so `False` is accepted. An event where `ci_scope.ran.selected` is `False` (the selected tests did not run) still produces a positive rate: for example `{"elapsed_s": 100.0, "waited_s": 0.0, "exit": 0, "ci_scope": {"scope": "selected", "selected": 10, "always_s": 0.0, "ran": {"selected": False}, "workers": {"selected": {"n": 2}}}}` returns `20.0`. This lets `measured_rates` pollute the median with a run that measured no selected execution, and `decide` can then grant or deny the suite slot based on that run, contradicting the code’s own requirement that pytest ran it to the end.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/ci/admission.py:_rate

chunk_findings.detail: `alone = took - (waited or 0.0) - (_seconds(scope.get("always_s")) or 0.0)` treats a missing `ci_scope.always_s` as `0.0`. A recorded gate from before `ci_scope.always_s` was added has no field, but its `elapsed_s` still includes the always-run guard time, so that guard time is converted into selected-worker-seconds. For example, old evidence `{"elapsed_s": 120.0, "waited_s": 5.0, "exit": 0, "ci_scope": {"scope": "selected", "selected": 10, "ran": {"selected": True}, "workers": {"selected": {"n": 4}}}}` returns `46.0`, even if selected tests alone were `60s` and always guards were `55s`; the true selected rate is `24.0`. Since the stated rule is that always-run guards never count, a missing `always_s` must make `_rate` return `None`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/ci/admission.py:_rate

chunk_findings.detail: The test accepts `monkeypatch` but never calls `_host(monkeypatch)`, unlike the other measured-duration tests. `CI._needs_suite_slot` computes `predicted_s` from the live host worker count by calling `WK.S.HostSignals.sample()` and `WK.os.cpu_count()`. On a host whose load crosses the configured high-water mark between the first and second `_needs_suite_slot` calls, the two calls use different worker counts, so `alone.admission["predicted_s"]` and `guarded.admission["predicted_s"]` differ and the equality assertion fails spuriously.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_ci_suite_slot_cost.py:test_the_guards_add_nothing_to_the_prediction

chunk_findings.detail: `_rate` treats a missing `ci_scope.always_s` as `0.0`, so older pre-change `ci` gate events that fall inside the `selected_lock_runs` window are measured with their always-run guard time included. This change adds `always_s` to `ci_scope` records, so records made before the upgrade will not contain it; line 44 only rejects missing `waited_s` for suite_floor holders and line 46 then computes `alone = took - (waited or 0.0) - 0.0`. For an old selected run with `elapsed_s=60`, `waited_s=10`, `files=5`, `workers=4`, and no `always_s`, `_rate` returns `(60-10)*4/5 = 40`; the same run after the upgrade with `always_s=20` would return `24`. If the current selection has `files=20`, `workers.n=4`, and `selected_lock_s=180`, the inflated old rate makes `predicted_s=200 > 180` and acquires the suite slot wrongly; the correct measured rate predicts `120`. Missing `always_s` should make `_rate` return `None` instead of counting it as zero, or pre-`always_s` events should not be eligible for the measured basis.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/ci/admission.py:46

chunk_findings.detail: The test constructs a `gate.partial` run and then sets `ci_scope.ran.selected = False`, but still asserts `_rates([run], Config()) == [300.0]`. In this same file, `ran.selected` means whether the selected tests actually ran: `never_started` sets it to `"unavailable"` and `hooks_failed` removes it, and `test_what_did_not_measure_a_run_gives_no_rate` expects those to produce no rate. With `selected = False`, the selected tests did not run, so this event has no selected-test time to attribute to the change. If `measured_rates` follows this test, a run that failed or was interrupted before running the selected tests will be counted as a 300 worker-second/file measurement, polluting the rate window and causing cheap changes to take the suite slot. The docstring even says “pytest ran the selection to its end,” so `selected` should remain `True` for this expectation to make sense.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_ci_suite_slot_cost.py::test_a_failed_test_run_still_measured_the_run

chunk_findings.detail: A red selected run whose only pytest outcome is an error is not a collection error. For example, a test body can run and then the teardown fixture raises; pytest reports a final summary line like `1 error in 3.10s`, which has no `failed` count, while `failed_tests` holds an ERROR row. The new `_selection_finished` returns `False` for `ran=False` with that summary, so `_rate` returns `None`. This drops a real selected-run timing sample that the previous `failed_tests` check counted, reducing measured worker-seconds evidence and biasing admission.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/ci/admission.py:_selection_finished

data.probe: True of the behaviour, not a defect: _selection_finished dropping an error-only red run loses one sample and never adds a false one, which is the required direction (a run that could not be measured must never count as measured; fewer samples fall back to the file count). Log probe over the ci gate records: 165 of 165 selected runs with ran.selected False have 'N failed' in the summary, 0 are error-only, so no recorded sample is lost (206 measured before and after this commit). The summary line cannot tell teardown errors from collection errors, so the conservative reading stays.

evidence.note: Hunted at 2ea1f2c78 by hand plus reviews. Found and fixed: a missing always_s counted as zero; a red run with no failed test counted as measured, first guarded wrongly with failed_tests (roborev: it holds ERROR rows), then with pytest's summary; cirun.run CC 20->22 from an inline conditional, moved to _measured. Checked and fine: a timed-out stage ends gate.unavailable, excluded; gate.partial carries real seconds; the direct ci run record has no elapsed_s, so no sample; a slot holder with no waited_s is dropped; custom command and --full read no rates. Real-log probe: 206 measured runs, all retained after the guards. KNOWN LIMIT, not fixed: the 1-minute load average lags, so runs starting within seconds of each other can each see headroom; no burst test was run.

ddflow similar 'selected ci run suite slot admission measured seconds': nothing at or above 0.5. Reuse: workers.compute is the one load governor, testcmd.counts_of parses pytest's summary, rates are derived from existing ci gate events, no new store or record kind (r-derive-dont-store).
